Chapter1/01_00_Introduction.notes: Stage 3.1 setup reviewed blobs/Chapter1/01_00_Introduction.md and judged the blob formalizable enough to receive its own scaffolding issue after the import skeleton lands. Candidate claims: (1) every field contains exactly one prime field, determined by its characteristic; (2) finite extensions of Q are number fields and arise as Q[x]/(f) for maximal ideals generated by monic irreducibles; (3) F_q[t] shares the PID/dimension-one/residue-field pattern of Z; (4) global function fields are finite extensions of F_q(t). Later completion/local-field survey sentences should stay as comments or deferred claims inside that file rather than blocking the scaffold.

claims.text: Every field contains exactly one prime field, namely Q in characteristic zero or F_p in characteristic p.
claims.reason: This is a mathematical characterization with direct existing infrastructure for characteristic and prime fields.

claims.text: Finite extensions of Q are number fields and can be presented as Q[x]/(f) for maximal ideals generated by monic irreducible polynomials.
claims.reason: This is a standard definitional/existence claim around number fields and quotient presentations.

claims.text: F_q[t] is a PID of dimension one and quotients by irreducibles yield finite residue fields F_(q^d).
claims.reason: This is a bundled mathematical package that can be scaffolded as statements/examples even if some proofs are deferred.

claims.text: Global function fields are finite extensions of F_q(t).
claims.reason: This is a clean definitional statement suitable for a scaffold file.

claims.text: The completions of Q are R and the p-adic fields Q_p.
claims.reason: Mathematical, but it depends on later local-field/completion infrastructure and should not be the first declaration in the opening-batch scaffold.
